title: Database languages and transaction control
summary: Distinguish DDL, DML, DCL, TCL, client commands, and parameterized SQL.
intro: Database-language categories describe the purpose of a statement, not separate databases or guaranteed transaction rules. A backend sends statements through a driver, and the driver and server each have responsibilities that must not be confused.
outcomes: Distinguish SQL commands from client script delimiters.
Explain parameter binding, least privilege, and commit boundaries.

sections.title: 1. Classify by purpose
paragraphs: DDL defines objects, DML retrieves or changes data, DCL manages access, and TCL governs transaction boundaries. Some courses call SELECT DQL; other classifications include it in DML. Explain the convention rather than claiming one list is a universal parser rule.

These labels do not say whether an operation can be rolled back. Oracle DDL normally creates implicit commit boundaries. PostgreSQL supports transactional behaviour for many DDL commands, with command-specific exceptions. Consult the actual command and connection behaviour before using rollback as a safety assumption.

sections.title: 2. The unit of work belongs to a session
paragraphs: Auto-commit can make each successful statement its own transaction. With explicit transactions, the application decides when a related group succeeds. A savepoint names an intermediate position so that part of the work can be undone while earlier work remains pending.

A transaction is not the same as a connection: one connection can run many transactions. An exception can leave a transaction needing an explicit rollback. Keep transactions short enough to avoid unnecessary locks and retained snapshots. Detailed isolation and schedules are developed in Unit 5.

sections.title: 3. A delimiter is not a database operation
paragraphs: The semicolon usually terminates a statement in a script. Oracle SQL*Plus SET SERVEROUTPUT ON and the slash on its own line are client instructions; slash submits the buffered PL/SQL block. MySQL DELIMITER changes how its command-line client splits compound statements. SQL Server GO separates client batches.

A database driver commonly expects the statement text without client commands. Copying a full terminal script into an API call can therefore fail even when the procedural body is valid. Separate the server statement from the client wrapper when integrating a lab into a backend.

sections.title: 4. Bind values; do not assemble executable text
paragraphs: A bound parameter is a value supplied separately through the driver. The DBMS does not interpret the value as SQL syntax. Concatenating an untrusted value into a WHERE clause allows its characters to become executable syntax. Quoting manually is not a replacement for driver-supported binding.

Bind values, not arbitrary object names or SQL keywords. Dynamic identifiers require an allow-list and proper identifier handling. Parameterization also does not grant permissions: the connected database identity still needs only the privileges the application requires.
sections.code:
SELECT student_id, name FROM U3Student
WHERE student_id = $1;

postgresql.code:
SELECT student_id, name FROM U3Student
WHERE student_id = $1;
postgresql.note: Driver template, not a standalone runnable script: bind an integer value using your database library. Parameter styles are driver-dependent.

WHERE student_id = :student_id;

sections.title: 5. Access control and backend boundaries
paragraphs: An owner account used for migrations should not automatically be the everyday application account. A reader may need SELECT on a limited view but no UPDATE on its base tables. GRANT gives a privilege within the product's role and ownership model; REVOKE removes a grant but may not remove other access paths.

SQLite does not offer a server-side GRANT/REVOKE user system comparable to PostgreSQL or Oracle; application and file permissions matter there. A stored procedure is not automatically safe merely because callers cannot see its SQL. Its execution rights, dynamic SQL, and input checks require explicit design.

revision: Classify a statement without inferring its commit behaviour.
Remove client-only commands when sending SQL through a driver.
Bind values and separate migration, runtime, and reader privileges.

questions.question: Is SELECT DML or DQL?
answer: Both classifications occur in teaching. DQL emphasizes retrieval; the broader DML category includes querying in many references. State which convention you are using and describe the operation rather than treating the acronym as a runtime property.

questions.question: Why is BEGIN not portable transaction-start syntax?
answer: PostgreSQL and SQLite accept BEGIN for a transaction. In Oracle PL/SQL it begins a procedural block; in SQL Server BEGIN begins a block unless followed by TRANSACTION. MySQL START TRANSACTION avoids confusion with stored-program blocks.

questions.question: Can a bound table name replace an allow-list?
answer: Ordinary value placeholders do not stand for table identifiers. Choose a permitted identifier through an allow-list and product-aware quoting, while binding data values separately. This preserves the boundary between code structure and data.
